title: Morocco Creates First-Ever AI Ministry, Targets $10 Billion in Economic Gains by 2030
key_facts: King Mohammed VI appointed Ahmed Rahhou on Friday 16 Oct 2026 as minister of artificial intelligence, digital transformation and administrative reform in the new government led by Fatima Zahra El Mansouri.

The article says the move brings AI into the official name of the ministry responsible for digital transformation and administrative reform; Rahhou inherits the Morocco Digital 2030 strategy and the Morocco AI 2030 roadmap ('AI Made in Morocco').
The roadmap aims to add MAD 100 billion ($10 billion) to GDP by 2030, create 50,000 direct and indirect jobs and train and certify 200,000 people in AI skills.
The government names digital sovereignty as a central priority: more control over the infrastructure, data and computing needed for AI.
In September authorities presented progress including more JAZARI Institutes for AI research, a sovereign AI marketplace and the Idarati AI assistant for administrative procedures.
Morocco is also working on AI models adapted to Arabic, Moroccan Darija and Amazigh.

A July 2026 IMF report found Sub-Saharan Africa ranked lowest on its AI Preparedness Index; only 38% of Africans used the internet in 2024 versus 68% globally, and Africa hosts about 5.5% of the world's data centers.
The article says success will depend on implementation of the roadmap and sustained investment.
quote_evidence: King Mohammed VI appointed Ahmed Rahhou as minister of artificial intelligence, digital transformation, and administrative reform on Friday, October 16, as part of the new government led by Fatima Zahra El Mansouri.
The strategy aims to generate MAD 100 billion ($10 billion) in additional gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030.
The new department brings artificial intelligence into the official name of the ministry responsible for digital transformation and administrative reform
why_it_matters_hint: Morocco is giving AI its own place in the cabinet while setting 2030 targets, but the article itself says delivery depends on investment and implementation.
notes: The headline calls it a 'first-ever AI ministry', but the article's own text says AI is added to the name of the existing digital transformation and administrative reform ministry; the entry words it that way. Targets are government goals.
